zh.question: 从表面一直往中心走，八个世界里面会遇到同样的东西吗？哪些是证据支持的结构，哪些还只是可能的模型？
zh.observe: 先拖动三维近景，从不同角度看同一处地形；再切到整球剖面，从外层逐步移到正中心。暂停并点选各层，比较地球的固态地幔、液态外核与固态内核，再看木星的混合中心。最后比较土卫六与巨蟹座 55 e，并读候选结构的证据说明。

academic.title: 整颗世界的剖面：地面、地幔和核心并不相同
academic.body:
水星、金星、地球和火星都是岩石行星，但岩石壳层和金属内部的比例与状态不同。水星的金属核占很大比例，MESSENGER 的引力与自转资料还给出固体内核证据；金星预计有岩石地幔和富铁核，但目前不能把固态、液态部分画成已经确定的两圈。地球的地幔主要为固体岩石，能在地质时间尺度缓慢流动，不能说整片地幔都是岩浆；外核为液态富铁合金，内核则主要为固体，说明相态同时取决于压力、温度和成分。

InSight 让火星的内部不再只靠整体密度猜测。2025 年 Bi 等人的地震研究报告固体内核的证据，推断半径约 600 千米；它更新了早先核模型，但精确尺寸、成分与核上过渡结构仍需检查。图中的火星内核因此标出新研究解释，不把剖面当实拍。

整球剖面从外缘走到正中心，层色用于区分材料，薄地壳经过放大。地球海水只在表面盆地里，土卫六甲烷湖也是局部液体，都不画成包住整个天体的厚内部壳。近景可看地形和液面，内部图可看层次；两种视图回答不同尺度的问题。

academic.title: 巨行星与冰卫星：模糊分界和正在改变的证据
academic.body:
木星云顶不是固体地面，向下进入越来越稠密的氢氦物质；高压下存在导电金属氢的解释。Juno 的引力数据支持一些具有弥散核心的模型：重元素富集区向外混合，未必像一个边缘清楚的硬核。海王星的“冰巨星”称呼不意味着可着陆的冰壳或已经证实的纯水海洋。引力、磁场和物性模型对高压混合内部提供约束，但 2025 年研究仍允许富水与富岩等多种结构；示意边线并不保证真实界面同样锐利。

土卫六是土星的卫星。Cassini 已观测其极区的甲烷、乙烷湖海，水冰则构成外壳。表面湖与深处可能的液态水必须分开。Petricca 等人在 2025 年重新分析潮汐引力响应，指出强耗散难以与全球地下海洋相容，提出接近熔点的高压冰及液水囊模型。本图展示这一候选解释，保留不确定标识，而不把旧有的全球地下海或新模型写成直接见到的事实。

academic.title: 系外行星与观察边界：看到中心不等于知道答案
academic.body:
巨蟹座 55 e 是紧靠恒星的岩石系外行星。Webb 热辐射与光谱约束可能的大气及极热表面，使白昼侧熔融硅酸盐海成为有依据的解释；这不是已经拍摄的海岸或测量出的海底。质量、半径和光谱不能唯一决定深处的成分和固液分布。剖面中的热表层、硅酸盐内部与候选金属核只是一种讲解方案，全部标为不确定；热色带不表示全球等厚熔融，底边也不表示岩浆海底位置。

地球和火星可利用地震波，其他世界还依靠引力、磁场、自转、潮汐、光谱及高压实验来反演内部。这些方法约束的是模型，不是透视照片。三维拖动改变观察角度；层间移动只是解释材料顺序，不表示真实探测器能穿过岩石、金属或高压流体，更不表示已经测得图中每一层的厚度。

zh.misconception: 看见云顶不等于找到地面；很热不一定全部是液体；走到图中中心不代表那里的结构已经被直接看见。甲烷湖、海水和熔融岩石不是同一种液体。
zh.boundary: 八个世界显示为相同大小。景观与三维内部都是程序示意，不是测绘地图或透视照片；层厚、颜色、移动速度与核心尺寸没有按观测标尺绘制。木星的弥散区与海王星内部边界可能渐变；金星核、火星新内核解释、土卫六深处及巨蟹座 55 e 内部保留各自证据限制。候选结构可以一路探索到中心，但不是已测深的航线。

narration.label: 把地球打开，一直看到中心
narration.text: 先用手指轻轻拖动画面，从另一边看看同一片地形。再把整颗地球打开一道口，开始我们的想象旅行。最外面是薄薄的岩石地壳，大陆和海底都有它。接着是很厚的地幔：岩石很热，大部分却仍是固体，只能在非常长的时间里慢慢变形。再往里，外核是会流动的金属；到了正中心，内核又是固体，因为这里也被压得非常紧。现在暂停，把刚才走过的层找一找。海水只在表面，没有一直通到地心。
narration.cue: 拖动地球近景比较视角；切整球剖面，逐层暂停，最后到中心。回看外核与内核，辨认液态与固态。

narration.label: 换一个世界，里面也会变
narration.text: 水星有比较薄的岩石外衣和很大的金属内部；金星虽然很热，核心哪些地方会流动，科学家还在找答案。火星的小震动送来新线索，提示它中心可能有固体内核。再换到木星，条纹是云，可不是地板。往里越来越稠密，较重的成分可能和周围混在一起，不像果子里一颗整整齐齐的核。海王星也不是外面裹着滑冰场。原来，同样画成一个球，里面可以很不一样。
narration.cue: 比较水星、金星与火星的核心标识，再选择木星与海王星。拖转整球剖面，暂停在中心混合区域。

narration.label: 土卫六的湖和冰
narration.text: 土卫六绕着土星转，是一颗卫星。这里有湖岸，可是湖里不是水，而是甲烷和乙烷。水在这里反而冻成了硬冰。湖只在一些地方，没有包住整颗卫星。再看看冰下面。科学家曾经猜这里有一片很大的地下水海洋，新的线索却提示：也可能是接近融化的高压冰，夹着一些液态水。我们画出一种可能，让问号也留在这里。再往中心，是可能富含岩石的部分。
narration.cue: 拖看土卫六代表性湖岸；切剖面，从水冰外壳到高压冰候选层再到岩石核心，指出不确定标识。

narration.label: 很烫的远方，和还不知道的地方
narration.text: 最后到巨蟹座五十五 e。它很靠近自己的恒星，朝着恒星的一面，岩石可能都热得会流动了。可没有人在那里拍过海岸照片。我们的图可以继续走到中心，但画出来的层只是一个可能的答案：岩浆到底多深，里面的金属核长什么样，还不知道。科学家会听地震的消息，也会读光、引力和磁场带来的线索。今天最有意思的，不只是走到了哪里，还可以问：我们是怎么知道的呢？
narration.cue: 选择巨蟹座 55 e，检查各层的候选说明并到达中心；回到近景，保留非实拍与无已知海底说明。

en.question: If we travel from the exterior to the center, do all eight worlds contain the same things? Which structures are well supported and which remain candidate models?
en.observe: Drag the 3D close view to inspect the same terrain from different angles. Switch to the whole-world cutaway and travel from the exterior to the exact center. Pause and select layers: compare Earth’s solid mantle, liquid outer core and solid inner core, then Jupiter’s mixed center. Finally inspect Titan and 55 Cancri e with their evidence notes.

academic.title: Whole-world cutaways: crust, mantle and core are different
academic.body:
Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are rocky planets with different proportions and states of rocky and metallic material. Mercury has a large metal core, with MESSENGER gravity and rotation data supporting a solid inner core. Venus is expected to have a rocky mantle and iron-rich core, but separate solid and liquid core regions are not established. Earth’s mantle is mostly solid rock that can creep over geological times; it is not a global magma ocean. A liquid iron-rich outer core surrounds a solid inner core, showing that phase depends on pressure and composition as well as temperature.

InSight provides seismic constraints on Mars. Bi et al. (2025) reported evidence for a solid inner core about 600 km in radius, updating earlier core models. Dimensions, composition and core-overlying transitions still require testing. Its inner-core region is labeled as a new research interpretation rather than an interior photograph.

The whole-world section reaches the exact center. Colors distinguish materials and thin crusts are enlarged. Earth’s oceans occupy surface basins and Titan’s hydrocarbon lakes are local liquids; neither becomes a thick global interior shell. A close view explains terrain and liquid surfaces, while the cutaway explains internal regions.

academic.title: Giants and icy moons: mixed boundaries and changing evidence
academic.body:
Jupiter’s clouds are not a solid surface. Deeper hydrogen-helium material becomes dense, with conducting metallic hydrogen expected at high pressure. Juno gravity data support models with a dilute core: heavy material is mixed outward rather than necessarily confined to a sharply outlined solid kernel. Neptune’s ice-giant label does not establish a walkable ice shell or pure-water sea. Gravity, magnetism and material models constrain its high-pressure mixtures, but a 2025 study still permits both water-rich and rock-rich interiors. Drawn boundaries need not be sharp physical interfaces.

Titan is Saturn’s moon. Cassini observed mainly polar methane-ethane lakes, while water ice forms the exterior. Those surface liquids are separate from possible deep liquid water. Petricca et al. (2025) reanalyzed the tidal gravity response and found strong dissipation difficult to reconcile with a global subsurface ocean, favoring near-melting high-pressure ice with possible water pockets. This view adopts that candidate interpretation with uncertainty labels rather than treating either an ocean or the new model as directly seen.

academic.title: Exoplanet limits: reaching the drawn center is not measuring it
academic.body:
55 Cancri e is a rocky exoplanet very close to its star. Webb thermal emission and spectra constrain a possible atmosphere and extreme surface heat, motivating a dayside silicate magma ocean. This is not a photographed coast or measured sea floor. Mass, radius and spectra do not uniquely fix deep composition or phase. The hot exterior, silicate interior and candidate metal core are one explanatory arrangement, all marked uncertain. The outer color band is not a uniform global molten shell, and its bottom is not a measured magma-ocean boundary.

Earth and Mars can be studied seismically; gravity, magnetism, rotation, tides, spectra and high-pressure experiments also constrain worlds. These support interior models rather than transparent photographs. Dragging changes the viewing angle. Moving through layers explains material order, not a survivable spacecraft trajectory or measured thicknesses.

en.misconception: Cloud tops are not ground; hot material is not necessarily all liquid; reaching the drawn center does not mean its structure has been directly seen. Hydrocarbon lakes, seawater and molten rock are different liquids.
en.boundary: Worlds have equal display sizes. Terrain and 3D interiors are procedural illustrations, not measured maps or transparent photographs. Layer thickness, color, travel speed and core size are uncalibrated. Jupiter and Neptune may have gradual transitions. Venus’s core, Mars’s new inner-core interpretation, Titan’s depths and 55 Cancri e retain their specific evidence limits. A candidate model can reach the center without being a measured travel path.

narration.label: Open Earth and travel to its center
narration.text: Gently drag the picture to see the same terrain from another direction. Then open a cut through the whole Earth for an imaginary journey. First comes thin rocky crust, under both land and ocean. Next is the thick mantle: hot rock that is mostly solid, changing shape only over very long times. Farther in, the outer core is flowing metal. At the exact center, the inner core is solid again, under enormous pressure. Pause and find the layers we passed. Seawater stays near the exterior; it does not reach the center.
narration.cue: Drag Earth’s close view, then open the whole-world cutaway. Pause in each layer and reach the center; compare liquid outer core and solid inner core.

narration.label: Different worlds, different interiors
narration.text: Mercury has a thin rocky exterior and a large metallic interior. Venus is very hot, but scientists still investigate which parts of its core can flow. Marsquakes offer new clues that a solid inner core may lie at the center of Mars. Now try Jupiter: its stripes are clouds, not floors. Material becomes denser inward, and heavier ingredients may mix with their surroundings instead of making a neatly edged fruit stone. Neptune is not wrapped in an ice rink either. Worlds drawn as similar balls can be very different inside.
narration.cue: Compare Mercury, Venus and Mars core labels, then rotate Jupiter and Neptune cutaways and pause at their mixed central regions.

narration.label: Titan’s lakes and ice
narration.text: Titan travels around Saturn: it is a moon. Its lakes contain methane and ethane, not water. Water is frozen into hard ice here. Lakes occur in some places rather than wrapping the whole moon. What is below the ice? Scientists once inferred a large buried water ocean. New clues suggest another possibility: high-pressure ice near melting, with pockets of liquid water. We show a possible answer while keeping the question mark. Farther inward is a region that may be rich in rock.
narration.cue: Drag the representative lakeshore view. In the cutaway, follow the ice shell, candidate high-pressure ice and rocky core, pointing out uncertainty labels.

narration.label: A hot distant world, and what remains unknown
narration.text: Finally visit fifty-five Cancri e. It is so close to its star that rock on the star-facing side may become hot enough to flow. Nobody has photographed its shore. Our picture can continue to the center, but its layers are one possible answer. How deep the magma reaches and what a metal core might be like are still unknown. Scientists listen to seismic clues and read light, gravity and magnetic fields. The interesting question is not only where we went, but how we know what might be there.
narration.cue: Choose 55 Cancri e, inspect each candidate label and reach the center. Return to the close view with the illustration and unknown magma-floor caveats visible.
